patient.title: Nivolumab and selected platinum chemotherapy before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules, structures cells use during division. It can slow cancer growth but also harm healthy nerves, blood-forming cells and hair follicles. There are up to three planned doses.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Report numbness, tingling, fever, painful muscles, mouth sores or diarrhoea.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

items.text: Nivolumab helps immune cells recognise cancer; chemotherapy damages dividing cells. Your prescribed backbone is paclitaxel and carboplatin.

patient.title: Nivolumab, gemcitabine and cisplatin before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Rare serious lung or kidney injury

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Hearing changes or tinnitus, which can persist
Numbness or tingling, which can persist
Electrolyte changes and need for hydration

patient.title: Nivolumab, pemetrexed and carboplatin before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Pemetrexed
agents.explanation: Pemetrexed blocks several enzymes that use folate to make the building blocks of DNA and RNA. This can slow or stop cancer-cell growth. Healthy cells can also be affected. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce important toxicities and are part of treatment.
agents.watch: Take the prescribed folic acid and attend for B12. Report mouth sores, diarrhoea, a rash, breathlessness or reduced urine; check before taking ibuprofen or other non-prescription medicines.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Skin rash; rarely serious skin reactions

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are up to three planned doses, one in each neoadjuvant cycle before surgical review.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

patient.title: Nivolumab, pemetrexed and cisplatin before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Pemetrexed
agents.explanation: Pemetrexed blocks several enzymes that use folate to make the building blocks of DNA and RNA. This can slow or stop cancer-cell growth. Healthy cells can also be affected. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce important toxicities and are part of treatment.
agents.watch: Take the prescribed folic acid and attend for B12. Report mouth sores, diarrhoea, a rash, breathlessness or reduced urine; check before taking ibuprofen or other non-prescription medicines.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Skin rash; rarely serious skin reactions

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Hearing changes or tinnitus, which can persist
Numbness or tingling, which can persist
Electrolyte changes and need for hydration

additional_support: Take the prescribed folic acid, vitamin B12 and rash-prevention steroid plan; continue folic acid for 21 days after the final pemetrexed dose. Cisplatin needs hydration, electrolyte checks and monitoring of kidneys, hearing and nerves.
Nivolumab can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Report new symptoms promptly and carry your immune alert card for at least five months after the last dose.
The prescriber specifies doses, duration, rescue treatment and interactions; follow one reconciled prescription.
